synopses.short: Goldie on the two-way traffic between classical and popular music of Black British origin.
synopses.medium: Goldie on the two-way traffic between classical music and popular music of Black British origin: artists reaching for the orchestra, and composers reaching for the beat.
synopses.long:
Goldie traces the ways Black British artists have engaged with classical music, from early attempts to capture its atmosphere through sampling, to commissioning orchestral musicians and creating records shaped by classical forms and ideas. Through a series of carefully chosen pairings, he reveals how composers and performers across genres have drawn inspiration from the classical tradition and transformed it into something new.

Each pairing begins with a classical work before moving to its contemporary counterpart, uncovering connections between Elgar and Goldie’s Inner City Life, Ravel and Soul II Soul, and Samuel Barber and Massive Attack. Along the way, Goldie explores how Delibes’s celebrated Flower Duet found an unexpected new life in The Rapsody's Dear Mallika. The programme concludes with Górecki’s Symphony No. 3 and its direct influence on one of Goldie’s most personal and iconic recordings, Mother.

Music featured: Elgar, Nimrod from Enigma Variations; Goldie, Inner City Life; Ravel, Daphnis et Chloé; Soul II Soul, African Dance; Barber, Adagio for Strings; Massive Attack, Unfinished Sympathy; the Flower Duet from Delibes’s Lakmé; The Rapsody featuring LL Cool J, Dear Mallika; Górecki, Symphony No. 3; and Goldie, Mother.

synopses.short: Goldie on the two-way traffic between classical and popular music of Black British origin.
synopses.medium: Goldie traces how popular music of Black British origin, including drum and bass and grime, evolved from incorporating classical music to creating new hybrid orchestral forms.

synopses.medium: It's Great North Run weekend, so Josh has an hour of Northern bangers to keep you running. Plus Nathan Shepherd from 6 Music picks music from 2 of his favourite Northern bands
synopses.long:
The Great North Run is the world's biggest half marathon, with a route that spans Newcastle and South Shields. To celebrate the event, Josh plays music from great northern artists and bands (do you see what he did there?) including The Beatles, Arctic Monkeys, Lisa Stansfield, English Teacher, The KLF, Olive and more.

Nathan Shepherd from 6 Music's Indie Forever and New Music Fix picks 2 of his favourite northern running tracks. Plus listener Lewis drops by via voice note to talk about why music and running are a perfect combo.

synopses.long:
Milkweed + P*SS. We catch-up with two of our hot favourites at End of the Road festival. 

Milkweed are a duo making experimental folk music steeped in myth and memory. Their latest record, Remscéla, is a haunting and expansive work rooted in the prelude tales of the Táin Bó Cúailnge, an epic of Irish mythology, filtered through the language of Thomas Kinsella’s 1969 translation.

P*SS are the noisy, genre-bending four piece from Vancouver B.C., who are about to release their debut album for Sub Pop  you made me / skin on linen.

Featuring inspiring, enriching melodies from composers including Bax, Price, and Dvorak, and a chance to Find Your Focus for the morning with music by Belle Chen meant to capture the feeling of being carefree and optimistic. Sian ponders on the difference between our cultivated and wild sides while out to Take a Breath, and Professor Catherine Loveday joins the show to explain why singing to a baby might have more profound effects than we realise.

synopses.long: Afrodeutsche curates a rich and reflective selection of contemporary music, following a path through coastlines, quiet forests, musical riddles and moments of stillness. Featuring music by Duncan Moss, Peter Gregson, Thomas Hewitt Jones, Alexis Ffrench, and Fergus McCreadie, the programme also shines a light on BBC Introducing artist Robinson's Village. From meditative piano works and ambient soundscapes to jazz-inflected textures and atmospheric collaborations, this immersive hour concludes with Benjamin Rimmer's gentle reflection, Recollection.

synopses.short: Zakia provides the soundtrack for your dreams, with guest Nashville artist Willam Tyler.
synopses.medium: Zakia provides the soundtrack for your dreams with selections from all around the world. Plus, Nashville artist William Tyler joins to share his Dreambience mix.
synopses.long:
DJ, broadcaster, writer, and dreamer Zakia Sewell provides the soundtrack to your dreams - playing music to ease the mind, soothe the soul, and open portals to new dimensions…

This week Zakia takes us on a dreamy journey around the globe with her selections from music new, old and some reissues. The show includes songs from ESG, Vashti Bunyan, Meridian Brothers and Anna Domino.

Plus, we hear from Nashville guitarist and composer. William Tyler as he share his dreams of an old family home and it's importance in his life, along with dreams of travel to locations he has yet to visit. He also shares his Dreambience mix inspired partially by the soundtrack from the Shining and music free from the restraints of time and genre. 

We want to hear your dreams! Send in tales of your sleepy adventures to dreamtime@bbc.co.uk.

A Reduced Listening Production for BBC Radio 6 Music.
